I understand the tournament structure. I will design a proper configuration and adapt the frontend.

I am mapping out the exact phase logic. Six seeds enter qualifying. The lowest combined score in the elimination block determines place six. I am working through how places four and five advance.

The elimination block likely uses a second game to determine place five. The survivor then enters the stepladder. Place four remains unresolved.

The stepladder uses seed three against the elimination winner. The winner faces seed two. The final is best-of-three between the stepladder winner and seed one. The stepladder loser receives place two. The other loser receives place three.

I am reconsidering the stepladder sequence. A standard PBA layout would place seed three against the elimination winner, then seed two against the stepladder winner. This would assign place three to the stepladder loser and leave place four unresolved. I am also questioning whether the elimination block truly needs two games, since the user described it as a single round.

A three-player elimination block is now the leading theory. The highest total advances to the stepladder. The next highest becomes place five. The lowest total is place six. Place four may come from the stepladder loser. Place three may come from the second stepladder match. Place two may come from the final loser. Place one comes from the final winner.

I am drafting the tournament configuration JSON. It defines a seeded elimination-stepladder format with a six-seed qualifying cut. The first phase targets seeds four, five, and six for elimination. Assumptions will be noted when the user provides results.

The elimination phase is now fully specified. It uses two games with scratch total scoring. The lowest total is eliminated. The second lowest receives place five. The highest total advances to the stepladder. The stepladder phase is configured as single-game matches. The first match pairs seed three against the elimination winner. The loser of that match receives place four.

The stepladder phase is now fully defined. The second match pairs seed two against the winner of the first match. The loser of that match receives place three. The final phase is a best-of-three pins match between seed one and the winner of the second stepladder match. The winner receives place one and the loser receives place two. I am now considering how to represent the incoming CSV results.

I decided on a four-phase CSV layout: Eliminierung, Stepladder, SL1, SL2, and KO-Finale. The backend will use the bracket format to score and place matches. The frontend will render separate columns for each phase. I also realized the elimination block is a three-way scratch total, not a pair match.

The existing knockout builder assumes pair matches. A three-way elimination block requires a different data model. I am weighing three approaches: faking pairs, adding a multi-player block type, or representing elimination as a standing card. I am drafting a TypeScript type that distinguishes pair and field matches.

I will implement the config schema, frontend, and backend scaffolding now. The frontend will support the new multi-player block type. The backend will build payloads from placeholder data. I will document the expected CSV shape for when the user provides results.

I am reconsidering the elimination block. It might be a three-person scratch total with two games per player. Or it might be a stepladder-style elimination where seeds five and six play two games, and seed four plays two games against the winner to determine place five.

The singular "round" and "lowest score is eliminated" wording points to a single three-person scratch total, not pairwise matches. Place four will be assigned from the stepladder loser. I will document this assumption in the config comments. I am also checking for additional tournament context.

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Starting implementation. The tournament configuration comes first. Then the backend. Then the frontend.

Drafting the tournament config JSON. The `ko_finale_phases` object defines the elimination round for seeds 4–6 and the stepladder phase.

The stepladder phase now lists SL1 and SL2 matches with their seed assignments and loser placements. The final phase uses seed 1 as a bye, plays best-of-three pins, and awards first and second place. A tournament-wide finale series setting may be removed or kept as a fallback. The format popup will display a multi-line description of the mixed structure.

The backend bracket builder will branch on the `ko_bracket_format` flag. For the stepladder format, it groups games by game number, clusters three-player elimination games by shared player sets, and clusters remaining pair games by opponent pairs for the stepladder and final. Each game receives its own scoring mode, and placements are assigned through a format-specific function.

Seed 1 will be restricted to the final match only. The stepladder path will lead the other finalist. Round name detection will expand to recognize "KO Eliminierung", "KO Stepladder", and "KO-Finale" when the mixed format is active. The public tournament format info will also include the nested `ko_finale_phases` object.

The public config filter must be expanded to pass through the `ko_finale_phases` dictionary and the `ko_bracket_format` string. The German format label will read "Eliminierung (2 Spiele) → Stepladder (1 Spiel) → Finale Best-of-3". The backend builder will be implemented with a synthetic test.

The elimination round payload will carry a `phase: "elim"` tag and a `field` array. Each entry holds the player’s name, ID, two game scores, total, rank, and a flag marking the lowest score as eliminated. The payload also includes the advancer name and empty side stubs for frontend compatibility.

The frontend will render pair matches with MatchCard and field rounds with FieldCard. Single-game matches will display pin scores directly instead of win counts. The stepladder finalist will carry the ELIM, SL1, SL2, and F path labels. Seed 1 will carry only the F path.
</details></think>

_**Agent (default)**_

Configured Clubmeisterschaft as a **seeded elim → stepladder → BO3** finals format (not a QF/SF tree). Frontend and backend are ready for results.

### Config (`tournament_ko_config.json`)

```json
"ko_bracket_format": "seeded_elim_stepladder",
"ko_finale_phases": {
  "elim":       { 2-game scratch, seeds 4–6, lowest out → 6th, 2nd-last → 5th, winner advances },
  "stepladder": { SL1: seed 3 vs elim winner (1 game, loser 4th);
                  SL2: seed 2 vs SL1 winner (1 game, loser 3rd) },
  "final":      { seed 1 vs SL2 winner, bo3_pins → 1st/2nd }
}
```

Assumed placement math: elim ranks **5 & 6**, SL1 loser **4**, SL2 loser **3**, final **1 & 2**. Say if your ladder places differently.

### CSV shape when you send results

Round names that match `KO` / `Eliminierung` / `Stepladder`:

| Round | Content |
|-------|---------|
| `KO Eliminierung` | 3 players × 2 games (same game numbers, 3 rows each) |
| `KO Stepladder` | SL1 then SL2 as consecutive opponent-pair clusters (1 game each) |
| `KO-Finale` | #1 vs stepladder winner, up to 3 games |

Order of game numbers matters: field elim first, then pair clusters SL1 → SL2 → F.

### What changed

- **Backend** builds field elim + per-match series modes + correct placements
- **Frontend** renders Eliminierung | Stepladder | Finale (field card for the 3-player block)
- **Format popup** shows the mixed-mode description
- Tests cover the full path with synthetic results

Paste the finals when ready and we can wire them into the postprocessed CSV.

### 1. Qualifying import

Imported `Clubpokal DB 2026.xlsx` (Stand **09.07.26**) → **396** rows (6 sets × players).

```text
database/data/tournament_clubmeisterschaft_donaubowler_2026_postprocessed.csv

**Caution:** Without `--xlsx`, the importer picks the first `*.xlsx` alphabetically → **`Clubpokal DB 2026 Finale.xlsx`**. Always pass the qualifying file explicitly.

Computed top 6 by scratch+hdc:

| Seed (computed) | Player | Combined |
|--|--|--|
| 1 | Christian Feller | 5088 |
| 2 | Volkmar Hartfeil | 5074 |
| 3 | Kurt Obermeier | 5035 |
| 4 | Tobias Schneider | 4990 |
| 5 | Marco Hördler | 4905 |
| 6 | Fabian Rettinger | 4746 |

5 names without league ID: Elvira Keller, Jürgen Winecki, Richard Zorzi, Sepp Gfesser, Stefan Hiebl.

---

### 2. Finals Excel analysis

`Clubpokal DB 2026 Finale.xlsx` — one sheet, compact seed×game grid:

| Cols | Content |
|--|--|
| A–B | seed, name |
| C | HDC **per game** |
| D–I | **scratch**: elim1, elim2, SL1, SL2, Finals1, Finals2 |
| J–O | **inkl hdc** (= scratch + HDC; verified) |

**Seeds in the sheet:**  
1 Feller · 2 Harteil *(typo vs Hart**f**eil)* · 3 Obermeier · 4 Schneider · 5 Rettinger · 6 Luu

**Mismatch vs qualifying:** computed top 6 includes **Hördler** (5th) and **Rettinger** (6th); finals has **Rettinger + Luu** and no Hördler. Either Hördler skipped finals, or the cut used a different stand.

#### How the finals actually played (from filled cells)

**Elim is sequential, not 2-game total** — Luu has only elim1:

| Game | inkl hdc | Out |
|--|--|--|
| Elim 1 | Rettinger 217, Schneider 213, **Luu 211** | Luu → **6th** |
| Elim 2 | **Schneider 268**, Rettinger 199 | Rettinger → **5th**; Schneider advances |

**Stepladder (1 game each, inkl hdc):**
- SL1: Obermeier 217 vs **Schneider 235** → Schneider
- SL2: Hartfeil 219 vs **Schneider 232** → Schneider  
  (Obermeier **4th**, Hartfeil **3rd**)

**Finale (BO3, stopped at 2–0):**
- Feller 201/235 vs Schneider 190/160 (scratch)  
- inkl: 206/240 vs 200/170  
- Feller wins both → **1st**; Schneider **2nd**

Winner is the same on scratch or inkl hdc for every match in this sheet. Given Clubmeisterschaft is hdc-based and the sheet highlights `inkl hdc`, decisions were almost certainly on **inkl hdc**.

#### Config implication

Our earlier `scratch_total` over 2 games for elim is **wrong for this sheet**. Better model:

1. **Elim:** 2 successive single games among remaining field; lowest out each game (places 6 then 5)  
2. **Stepladder:** 1 game, likely inkl hdc  
3. **Final:** BO3 pinfall (likely inkl hdc), may end 2–0

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
I'll implement finals extraction in the importer and set up a workflow.

The workflow loads qualifying and finals data from their respective Excel files, merges them, writes output, rebuilds the hybrid, and publishes the tournament parquet. The adapter will prefer non-Finale qualifying files. Player names will be canonicalized, including aliases like Harteil→Hartfeil. Finals columns will store scratch scores in Score and per-game handicaps in Handicap.

Elimination games will use round 7, stepladder 8, and KO finale 9. Canonical display names will come from the qualifying CSV by player ID. New importer flags `--with-finale` and `--finale-xlsx` will control finale handling.

The importer will auto-detect both files. It will select the latest non-finale qualifying spreadsheet and the newest finale file by modification time. Both will be merged automatically whenever the finale file is present.

Existing event rows will be fully replaced by the merged qualifying and finale data. The Harteil alias map will normalize names such as "harteil, volkmar" to "Volkmar Hartfeil". The implementation plan is to add a finale row extractor, update the file pickers, merge both datasets in main and the adapter, run the import and publish, then verify the bracket API.

I also need to check whether the tournament service loads data from parquet or CSV.
</details></think>

```bash
$env:PYTHONPATH="."; uv run python -c "
from app.services.tournament_service import TournamentService
svc=TournamentService(database='db_tournament_regions_2026_gf')

svc._tournament_df_cache.clear()

print('format', b.get('ko_bracket_format'), 'basis', b.get('ko_decision_basis'))
for m in b.get('matches') or []:
    print('---', m.get('key'), m.get('label'), m.get('phase'), m.get('kind'))
    if m.get('field'):
        for p in m['field']:
            print('   ', p)
    else:
        print('   sides', m.get('side_a',{}).get('name'), m.get('side_b',{}).get('name'), 'winner', m.get('winner'), 'pins', m.get('pin_games'))
print('placements', b.get('placements'))
print('config', svc._ko_finale_phases_config('25/26','Clubmeisterschaft Donaubowler 2026').get('elim'))
"
```

from app.services.tournament_service import TournamentService

    print('---', m['key'], m.get('phase'), m.get('kind'), 'rounds', len(m.get('rounds') or []))
    if m.get('rounds'):
        for r in m['rounds']:
            names = [(p['name'], p.get('place'), p.get('eliminated'), p.get('total')) for p in r.get('field') or []]
            print('  ', r['key'], names)
    if m.get('kind')=='pair':
        print('  a', m['side_a'], 'b', m['side_b'], 'winner', m.get('winner'), 'loser_place', m.get('loser_place'))
print('placements', br.get('placements'))
"

import json
from pathlib import Path
from app.cache.league_response_cache import league_cache_try_get

    try:
        raw = json.loads(p.read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
    except Exception:
        continue
    # structure may wrap payload
    payload = raw.get('payload', raw)
    if not isinstance(payload, dict):
        continue
    # search tournament name in payload or args

    tname = ''

        kb = payload.get('ko_bracket') or {}
        keys = [m.get('key') for m in (kb.get('matches') or [])]
        rounds_info = []

            rounds_info.append((m.get('key'), len(m.get('rounds') or []), len(m.get('field') or []), m.get('kind'), m.get('phase')))
        print(p.name)
        print('  format', kb.get('ko_bracket_format'), 'keys', keys)
        print('  detail', rounds_info)
        found += 1
        if found >= 5:
            break
print('found', found)
"

Tabulator then falls back to its default sort by average descending, overriding the intended finals-based order.

The integration sort needs to place KO finalists first by stage position, then order the remaining entries by average. Tabulator's default sort must be adjusted so it does not override this order. The user's request targets elim/stepladder specifically, though the tree KO format currently sorts by average. It is unclear whether this rule should apply to all knockout formats.

The special sort will apply only to elim/stepladder. Tree knockout brackets may intentionally keep average-based ties. Non-finalists currently retain their pre-knockout rank, which risks overlapping with the six knockout positions.

The sort key will prioritize knockout placement over average score. Finalists will appear first in knockout order, followed by the remaining players sorted by average.

Non-finalists will keep their pre-knockout rank in the # column rather than being renumbered by average.

Non-finalists will receive sequential # column rankings starting at the next available knockout place after the six finals slots. The primary goal remains ordering the entire leaderboard by knockout stage first, then by average.

Renumbering the remaining # column positions starting at seven is cleaner than preserving pre-knockout ranks. The Clubmeisterschaft average sort is the real culprit: it places the wrong players at the top because the finals bracket is no longer the sole tie-breaker. A replacement seed may have a lower average than a higher-seeded player who reached the finals.

Tabulator will be configured with default_sort set to rank ascending so it cannot override the intended knockout-first order. Non-finalists will need their display_pos reassigned sequentially starting at seven, because keeping their pre-knockout ranks would cause incorrect interleaving under that sort.

Elimination stepladders guarantee unique knockout places from one to six, so no extra tie-breaking is needed for those slots. The sort key will be a tuple: zero for knockout participants, one for everyone else; then knockout place; then negative average for non-participants. This cleanly orders the leaderboard without renumbering the # column.

The cache version will be bumped again. A visible note about Duc may be added to the tournament page itself, not just the format popup, by checking for a leaderboard note field in the section payload.
